NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is the installation of pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment at the heat exchanger inlet to prevent biofilm and scale accumulation by disrupting microbial cell membranes and preventing crystal nucleation. Standard practice relies on periodic mechanical cleanings and limited chemical treatments that don't fully prevent fouling between interventions. Our PEF mitigation is a genuine departure as it provides continuous, non-chemical fouling prevention through electroporation of microorganisms and inhibition of scale formation. The closest existing practice is pulsed power water treatment in some industrial cooling systems, but those typically use lower frequencies and energies for general biocide purposes, whereas our approach specifically targets the plate heat exchanger geometry with optimized pulse parameters to maximize disruption of attachment points in confined channels.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation for biofilm prevention is the cell membrane breakdown electric field strength (E_c) ≈ 1-10 kV/cm, where the energy delivered per cell is U = ½C(V²) with C as cell membrane capacitance (~1pF). For our PEF system applying 5kV pulses at 100Hz for 1ms daily, the energy per pulse is 12.5 nJ, sufficient to rupture microbial membranes. For scale prevention, the critical supersaturation ratio (S_crit) is reduced by PEF treatment from ~1.5 to ~1.2, as confirmed by studies showing 40-60% reduction in crystal nucleation rates at these field strengths. This directly addresses the fouling driving mechanism by preventing both biological attachment and mineral precipitation.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
1. PEF generator unit (b) - replaces existing chemical injection pump
2. Pulse-forming network (b) - connects to generator
3. Treatment chamber (a) - installed at heat exchanger inlet using existing pipe
4. Electrodes (b) - installed in treatment chamber, standard stainless steel rods
5. Control system (b) - programmable logic controller with timer
6. Daily 1ms pulse protocol (c) - programmed into existing control system
7. Voltage monitoring (a) - connects to existing pressure/temperature monitoring system

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice includes: chemical injection system, monthly chemical dosing, quarterly mechanical cleaning, monitoring equipment.
Our intervention replaces: chemical injection system (b) with PEF generator (b)
Our intervention adds: treatment chamber (a), electrodes (b), control system (b)
Our intervention modifies: daily 1ms pulse protocol (c) instead of monthly chemical dosing
Burden comparison: Same installation complexity (pipe modification), same monitoring requirements, lower chemical consumption (eliminates biocides), reduced labor (no monthly chemical handling). Burden class is same as standard practice with reduced operational costs.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Install PEF system with monitoring on identical heat exchanger in parallel with existing unit. Run both under identical conditions for 6 months. Measure heat transfer coefficient (U) weekly using temperature sensors and flow meters. Pass criterion: PEF-treated unit maintains U > 2500 W/m²K throughout 6 months without chlorination. Fail criterion: PEF-treated unit drops below 2500 W/m²K at any point, or requires mechanical cleaning before 6 months. Kill criterion: if control unit (without PEF) maintains U > 2500 W/m²K for >12 months without cleaning, the intervention is invalidated. Test duration: 6 months minimum, extendable to 12 months if no failures occur.
